clue.text: Plays hard at first — further on they changed

definitions.note: plural because Shakespeare's history comes in two parts, so the title names a pair of plays

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word hard
changed tells us the letters of further on they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A remark that drama is tough at the start and gets altered as rehearsals go on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges FURTHERONTHEY into ENRYTHEFOURTH, after H from 'hard at first'. Shakespeare wrote this history in two parts, which justifies the plural 'Plays'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's history about Bolingbroke's reign is a pair of dramas, Part One and Part Two.

clue.text: Thunderous applause?

parts.note: the noise of thunder is called by the same word as a round of hand-slapping applause, so the clue reads as thunder applauding

explanation.definitionFit: A peal of thunder and a strike of palms together share one noun, so thunder's noise is pictured as applause.

clue.text: See 1
See 7
A couple of leading roles 1 3 has

definitions.text: A couple of leading roles 1 3 has

parts.words: A couple of leading roles 1 3 has
parts.note: parts here are the divisions of a play cycle rather than actors' roles; the history named at 1 and 3 is split into a first and a second instalment

explanation.surface: A remark about the two starring roles in a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roles' pushes towards actors' parts, but the parts meant are the two instalments of Shakespeare's history play.
explanation.definitionFit: The history is divided into two plays, labelled as the first and the second instalment of the drama.

clue.text: Newspaper editor's leader put in the last section from then on

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: put in means one group of letters is placed inside the word for the last section

parts.note: the rear is the hindmost section of anything
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

indicators.note: leader of a word is its first letter, here of editor's

explanation.surface: An instruction about where a newspaper places the editor's leading article in its pages.
explanation.walkthrough: The Financial Times is a London business daily. 'Newspaper editor's leader' reads like a leading article, but it supplies two separate pieces that go inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean subsequently, from that point in time onwards; a simple synonym.

clue.text: Eventual successor of 1 3, for example, in 15 theatre

definitions.meaning: ... Hal, heir to the throne and later Henry V, holds the heir's title in the plays
a playhouse in London's theatre district, on Coventry Street, carrying the heir's title as its name

explanation.surface: A remark about the heir in Shakespeare's history and a London playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Prince of Wales Theatre is a London playhouse in the West End, the answer to 15.
explanation.definitionFit: The title given to the heir to the English throne, held by Hal, and also the name of a London theatre.

clue.text: Puts a barrier around marine animals starting to smell?

parts.note: seals are sea mammals with flippers
food that is going off is beginning to smell bad

explanation.surface: A question whether sea creatures are being fenced in because they have begun to stink.
explanation.definitionFit: To close off an area is to block access by putting a cordon round it; idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Detest short cape on a bishop

indicators.note: on means the cape piece comes after the other letters in this down-reading across clue order

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: short means the word for the cape loses its final letter

parts.note: Cape Horn is the southern tip of South America

explanation.surface: A complaint about a bishop wearing a cape that is too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cape' looks like a garment but is the headland Horn; 'short' docks it to HOR, which follows A and B.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something strongly; a straight synonym for intense dislike.

clue.text: Drivers try to avoid this carriage

definitions.meaning: a speed camera set-up that catches motorists, which they would rather not drive into

explanation.surface: Motorists steer clear of a certain horse-drawn vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: A speed trap catches motorists; a pony trap is a small horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A police speed check is a snare drivers avoid, and the same word names a small horse-drawn cart.

clue.text: Transform later reign, making more changes

indicators.note: transform asks for the letters of later reign to be rearranged into a new shape

explanation.surface: A suggestion to transform a future monarchy by further reforms.
explanation.definitionFit: Modifying something again; to alter once more is to make further changes.

clue.text: Formality seen in most architecture

indicators.note: seen in means the answer is visible inside the words most architecture

explanation.surface: Stiff formality is characteristic of most buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiffness of manner, from the stiffening agent for collars; figurative synonym.

clue.text: Cost of journey in two parts, with profit reasonable, we hear

definitions.text: Cost of journey in two parts

parts.note: a return on an investment is the profit it yields

indicators.note: we hear means the next word is chosen for how it is pronounced, not spelt

parts.note: fair means reasonable or just

explanation.surface: A traveller notes that a there-and-back ticket gives decent value and a fair price.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket covering the outward trip and the trip back is priced as one two-leg charge.

clue.text: Fish around company laboratory for evidence of environmental friendliness

indicators.note: around means the fish's letters wrap the other pieces

parts.note: an eel is a snake-like fish

explanation.surface: Fishing near a firm's research lab turns up proof of green credentials.
explanation.definitionFit: A label certifying a product as green is a mark showing it is kind to nature.

clue.text: Part of our capital we dispatch over time

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: over means one word covers the other, so the time letter sits within the dispatch word

parts.note: to dispatch is to send off

explanation.surface: Londoners talk of dispatching something through a district over a period.
explanation.walkthrough: The West End is London's theatre and shopping district.
explanation.definitionFit: The western district of London, the British capital, famous for its theatres.

clue.text: No repetition of three points for which 5 22 could be 2 and 10

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: repetition of says the following letters come twice

parts.note: N, S and E are three compass points

explanation.surface: A clue that seems to be about scoring three points with no repeats.
explanation.walkthrough: Parts one and two of the word wanted could be 2 and 10, CLAP and TRAP, which join to make a word for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Claptrap is drivel, so this is a synonym for empty talk, defined by putting its two halves together.

clue.text: Literature's characters in 24 down, then across

definitions.meaning: as in a man of ..., a literary person
24 down then 24 across together spell the alphabet, whose characters are its written symbols

explanation.surface: Written characters in a crossword are read down and then across.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 24 down (ALPH) and then 24 across (ABET) gives ALPHABET.
explanation.definitionFit: Written symbols of the alphabet, and also learning or literature in the phrase man of letters.

clue.text: Soldier initially reading poem to sweetheart

indicators.note: initially picks out just the first letter of reading

parts.note: If is Kipling's famous poem
leman is an archaic word for a lover

explanation.surface: A soldier begins by reading verse aloud to a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If—' is a well-known Rudyard Kipling poem; LEMAN is an old word for a lover.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifleman is an infantry soldier armed with a rifle; specific example of a soldier.

clue.text: Tell the story of number again

definitions.meaning: to count a second time, as at an election

explanation.surface: Narrate the history of a figure once more.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrate in detail, and also count a second time, as votes are checked in a close election.

clue.text: Somehow use ten gears to drive away

indicators.note: somehow use asks for the letters of ten gears to be employed in some new arrangement

explanation.surface: Advice on using ten gears to motor off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somehow use' signals the anagram, so 'use' gives no letters: rearrange TEN GEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to push them away emotionally, causing separation.

clue.text: Puts on vehicles

definitions.meaning: stagecoaches, horse-drawn coaches on a route

explanation.surface: A producer mounts motor transport.
explanation.definitionFit: To mount a production on a theatre platform, and the old coaches that ran between staging posts.

clue.text: Take commercial break, having no anchor?

parts.note: an ad is a commercial
a rift is a break or split

explanation.surface: A suggestion to take an advert break during a TV programme with no presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anchor' suggests a news presenter, but the definition is a boat floating loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat floating loose without mooring; the question mark admits the definition by example.

clue.text: See 5
Very brief period in which play after interval is out of order

indicators.note: out of order means the two words of the phrase swap places

parts.note: the second half is the play after half-time

explanation.surface: During a football match, play after half-time is deemed against the rules.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out of order' swaps the halves of SECOND HALF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny instant, a fraction of a moment, like a split second.

clue.text: Take part in crime, a risky undertaking

parts.note: a bet is a gamble, a risky venture

explanation.surface: Joining in a crime is a risky business.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid or assist a wrongdoer, as in aiding and abetting.

clue.text: Poetic river visible in aerial photograph

indicators.note: visible in means the river is seen within the words aerial photograph

explanation.surface: A river in poetry shows up in a picture taken from the air.
explanation.walkthrough: Alph is the sacred river in Coleridge's poem Kubla Khan.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred river of Xanadu in Coleridge's Kubla Khan, so a river from verse.

clue.text: Hearing projections about line for some characters in 1 3 5 22 down

indicators.note: about means one piece is wrapped round the line letter

parts.note: ears are the organs of hearing that project from the head

explanation.surface: Projecting ears hear something about a line.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry IV features the Earls of Worcester, Northumberland, Douglas and Westmoreland.
explanation.definitionFit: Several noblemen in the two Henry plays hold this rank, such as Northumberland and Worcester.

clue.text: My first is a lot of fresh information, my second's a climber's destination, my whole is a language for thought domination

parts.note: news is fresh information
a mountain climber aims for the peak

explanation.surface: A riddle in rhyme: first part, second part, and the whole word.
explanation.walkthrough: Newspeak is the controlled language in Orwell's Nineteen Eighty-Four.
explanation.definitionFit: The propaganda language devised by Orwell's regime to restrict what people can think.
